# Motivation and Review

Let's simply recall everything from the [prior module](07_Homework.qmd) and the related resource [https://tgstewart.cloud/ipm/interactions.html](https://tgstewart.cloud/ipm/interactions.html), which gives us reasoning for pursuing this. We'll continue working with the NHANES data and the same variables of interest. Toward the end of the module we observed two things:

1. Lasso zeroes out individual coefficients, so a group can end up "partially pooled", for example, the race group of 'Hispanic' could end up with 2/4 deviation terms. That doesn't have a clean meaning when we're working with the coefficients, so we'd prefer to have a "group lasso" penalty that could zero things out altogether!

2. If we have more than 2 groups, there's a lot of possible sharing structures between full sharing (all one model) and no sharing (all separate models). Shrinking toward the average doesn't reveal a potential structure like for the race group like 'Hispanic and Mexican share a curve', but "fusion" can do this!

So let's explore both of these methods.

# Group Lasso

Let's start with recalling the lasso formula

$$\hat{\beta}_{\text{lasso}} = \underset{\beta}{\arg\min}\  \|Y - X\beta\|_2^2 + \lambda\|\beta\|_1$$
where $\|\beta\|_1 = \sum_j |\beta_j|$ is the $L_1$ norm. 

A key attribute of the lasso is that some coefficients are exactly zero, so variable selection is performed.

Previously, we were cool with that in general, but now we have blown up our model with interaction terms and groups and we want to be a little bit more strategic about which terms we drop. For example, if we're going to drop the terms for $Age*I(hispanic)$ and $Age^2 * I(hispanic)$, then we may want to just drop all the terms associated with $I(hispanic)$ from the model, or remove the group. An example full interaction model with `Race1` like the one described is shown below:

$$\begin{align*}
E[\text{BPSysAve}\mid \text{age}, \text{race}] & = \beta_0 + \beta_1\,\text{age} + \beta_2\,\text{age}^{\prime} + \beta_3\,\text{age}^{\prime\prime}\\
&+ \beta_4\,I(\text{hispanic}) + \beta_5\,\text{age}\cdot I(\text{hispanic}) + \beta_6\,\text{age}^{\prime}\cdot I(\text{hispanic}) + \beta_7\,\text{age}^{\prime\prime}\cdot I(\text{hispanic})  \\
&+ \beta_8\,I(\text{mexican}) + \beta_9\,\text{age}\cdot I(\text{mexican}) + \beta_{10}\,\text{age}^{\prime}\cdot I(\text{mexican}) + \beta_{11}\,\text{age}^{\prime\prime}\cdot I(\text{mexican})  \\
&+ \beta_{12}\,I(\text{white}) + \beta_{13}\,\text{age}\cdot I(\text{white}) + \beta_{14}\,\text{age}^{\prime}\cdot I(\text{white}) + \beta_{15}\,\text{age}^{\prime\prime}\cdot I(\text{white})  \\
&+ \beta_{16}\,I(\text{other}) + \beta_{17}\,\text{age}\cdot I(\text{other}) + \beta_{18}\,\text{age}^{\prime}\cdot I(\text{other}) + \beta_{19}\,\text{age}^{\prime\prime}\cdot I(\text{other})  \\
V[\text{BPSysAve}\mid \text{age}, \text{race}] & = \sigma^2
\end{align*}$$
